title: Tablet navigation hides its only accessible link names
trigger: Open the demo at a viewport between 761 and 979 CSS pixels wide, then navigate the desktop icon rail using a screen reader or inspect its accessibility tree.
expected: Overview, Health records, Appointments, Medical profile, Log a symptom, and Settings retain descriptive accessible names when their visible text is collapsed.
actual: The tablet media query sets .nav-item span and .sidebar-log span to display:none. App.tsx supplies names only inside those spans and no aria-label/title on the six links; the remaining Lucide SVGs have no title text. The rail remains visible and keyboard-focusable but its destination names are removed from the accessibility name computation.
impact: Screen-reader users at the tablet breakpoint encounter unnamed primary navigation and symptom/settings actions. The visible icon rail also provides no tooltip labels.
evidence: Source proof: apps/web/src/styles/layout.css:317-337 and App.tsx:108-135. Saved screenshot evidence/ui/demo-profile-768.png visibly shows the icon-only rail; matching DOM confirms the anchors have no explicit names. r2-ui-matrix.jsonl uses DOM text content for its label inventory and does not establish computed accessible names. Codex requested a bounded accessibility-tree confirmation from the coordinator; no new UI run is claimed here.
smallestFix: Add stable aria-label values to the navigation and symptom/settings anchors, or keep their text visually hidden with a screen-reader-visible technique rather than display:none. Optional tooltips can help sighted users without replacing accessible names.
regressionCheck: At 768 CSS pixels assert the accessibility-tree link names for all six rail actions and keyboard activation destinations; recheck 375 and 1440 to avoid duplicate or missing names.

title: Selected source text becomes dark text on a dark selection background
trigger: Select or keyboard-highlight a passage in a record, brief, or other selectable browser text.
expected: Selected medical text remains legible while the user reviews or copies it.
actual: The global ::selection rule uses --ink (#342B2C) over --accent-text (#8C2F3B). Relative-luminance arithmetic from those exact sRGB values gives a 1.6917:1 foreground/background ratio, while white over the same background gives 8.1243:1.
impact: Highlighting source words makes them substantially harder to read, especially when checking doses or values before copying. Normal unselected body text is unaffected.
evidence: Exact source: apps/web/src/styles/tokens.css:12,17,117-119. Codex continuation computed luminance directly from these constants using the sRGB linearization formula; this is arithmetic evidence, not a runtime screenshot or assistive-technology test. Coordinator was asked for selection-style confirmation.
smallestFix: Use the existing white surface/button-text token for selected text on the deep-red background, preserving the approved palette.
regressionCheck: Select a source passage and inspect both rendered colors; verify readable selected foreground/background and unchanged regular text in supported browsers.
